variant_decisions.evidence: ASV's text renders a verb of writhing pain -- 'My anguish, my anguish! I am pained at my very heart' -- which is the ketiv אחולה (root חיל). The qere אוֹחִילָה 'I will wait' is what the mapped textual_variant note relegates to the margin: 'Another reading is, I will wait patiently'. Text and note together put the ketiv in the ASV's line and the qere in its margin.

ASV reads 'because thou hast heard, O my soul' -- a second feminine singular addressed to the soul, which is the qere שָׁמַעַתְּ. But the ketiv שמעתי differs only by the final yod of the archaic 2fs perfect ending and can be read as the same 'thou hast heard'; the English therefore does not exclude it. The one note bearing on the alternative, 'Or, as otherwise read, my soul heareth', is classed alternative_rendering and decides nothing. Both readings retained; the qere base fallback carries the projection.
